name: Iowa
tagline: From the Loess Hills to the Mississippi bluffs, past covered bridges and Amish farms.
intro: Iowa's byways climb the windblown Loess Hills above the Missouri, cross the farm middle of the state on the old Lincoln, Jefferson and White Pole highways, and wind through the unglaciated Driftless corner to the Mississippi bluffs. This chapter follows the Iowa Byways Program, begun in 1988 and run by the Iowa Department of Transportation, which counts 14 byways, three of them national (Loess Hills, the Great River Road and the Lincoln Highway). Two routes that retrace early auto trails, the Lincoln and Jefferson highways, carry the title Heritage Byway rather than Scenic Byway.

members.name: Great River Road National Scenic Byway
members.blurb: The Iowa stretch of the Mississippi river road follows green pilot-wheel markers some 355 miles from Keokuk to New Albin, past barges at the lock and dam sites and the animal-shaped mounds of Effigy Mounds near Harpers Ferry.

members.name: Lincoln Highway Heritage Byway
members.blurb: Iowa's share of the 1913 coast-to-coast road crosses the state from Council Bluffs to Clinton through towns U.S. 30 later bypassed, past Preston's gas station in Belle Plaine and the restored Reed-Niland Corner at Colo.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Loess Hills National Scenic Byway
members.blurb: The main route runs 220 paved miles from the Missouri line below Hamburg north to Akron along bluffs of windblown silt, and gravel excursion loops lead off to the prairie of Broken Kettle Grasslands near Sioux City.

members.name: Covered Bridges Scenic Byway
members.blurb: An 82-mile route out of Winterset, where a limestone courthouse holds the square, runs like wheel spokes to the red covered bridges of Madison County, Holliwell and Imes among them, and past John Wayne's birthplace.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Delaware Crossing Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A 36-mile loop over the limestone-bluffed Maquoketa River valley of Delaware County, by the trout hatchery built at Manchester in 1897 and the old Lenox College campus at Hopkinton, now a museum.

members.name: Driftless Area Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A 144-mile zigzag over the unglaciated hills of Allamakee and Winneshiek counties, down to trout streams and past stone churches, from the effigy mounds near Harpers Ferry to the Norwegian-American museum in Decorah.

members.name: Glacial Trail Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A 36-mile loop along the Little Sioux River around Peterson and Linn Grove, where steep unplowed prairie hills flank a valley cut by glacial meltwater and the Prairie Heritage Center explains the kames and kettles the ice left.

members.name: Grant Wood Scenic Byway
members.blurb: About 80 miles from Stone City, where Grant Wood helped found an art colony, east through Anamosa and Maquoketa to Bellevue on the Mississippi, among limestone bluffs and past a castle-like penitentiary that still holds inmates.

members.name: Historic Hills Scenic Byway
members.blurb: About 105 miles of wooded hills in southeast Iowa, where horse-drawn buggies share the road near Drakesville and Bloomfield and the route passes Iowa's oldest courthouse and the site of its only Civil War battle.

members.name: Iowa Valley Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A 77-mile drive down the Iowa River from the edge of the Meskwaki Settlement to the Amana Colonies, through the Czech farm towns of the Bohemian Alps and past Lily Lake, where American lotus blooms in July.

members.name: Jefferson Highway Heritage Byway
members.blurb: Two-lane roads roughly along U.S. 65 and 69 from Northwood to Lamoni follow the old Winnipeg-to-New Orleans motor route, past courthouse squares and the restored gas and lodging stop at Reed-Niland Corner in Colo.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: River Bluffs Scenic Byway
members.blurb: About 109 miles through the Turkey and Volga river country of Fayette and Clayton counties, past Motor Mill and Governor Larrabee's house at Montauk, to Pikes Peak State Park above McGregor and its view into three states.

members.name: Western Skies Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Highway 44 and county roads carry this 142-mile route from Missouri Valley to Stuart, through Danish Elk Horn with its working windmill and the German church towns of Westphalia and Panama.

members.name: White Pole Road Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Twenty-six miles of old U.S. 6 run beside Interstate 80 between Adair and Dexter on a road lined with white-painted telephone poles, from a Jesse James train-robbery site to a Barrow Gang shootout site.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).
